To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CSDs in auditory cortex and the inferior colliculi are composed of a series of excitatory synaptic potentials with a spatio-temporal organization that is similar to that found in other sensory neocortical and subcortical areas.

the CSD method permits the functional identification of the depth locations of specific anatomical laminae and that it provides a spatio-temporal analysis of the synaptic activities of the auditory midbrain and cortex.
the CSD method permits functional identification of recording locations in the inferior colliculi and auditory cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional anatomy of the auditory midbrain and auditory cortex.
the functional identification of anatomical structures and the determination of the spatio-temporal distribution of synaptic activity within these structures.
the development and application of a physiological method of functional identification of recording locations in brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CSD analysis of click-evoked responses provides a very useful tool for the functional identification and localization of recording sites in both the auditory midbrain and auditory cortex.
the CSD profiles in both the inferior collicular and auditory cortical areas reflect in great detail the functional organization of the auditory system.
the CSD method is a valuable tool for the functional identification and analysis of neuronal activity in the inferior colliculi and auditory cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CSD profiles in the auditory cortex are very similar to the profiles obtained from other sensory areas of the cortex and that the CSDs in central nucleus of the IC are very similar to CSDs obtained from the visual cortex.

in both the inferior colliculi and the auditory cortex the spatio-temporal profiles of the synaptic activities are very similar and can be interpreted in terms of anatomical and physiological principles.
the CSD method is a powerful tool for the identification of the functional anatomy of the inferior and superior auditory areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CSD analysis of the field potential can be used as an alternative to the invasive recording of single units.
the functional anatomy of the auditory midbrain and cortex can be studied in vivo in awake animals by using current source density (or current source analysis) as an analytical tool.
CSD analysis can be used to identify specific functional sites in the auditory system.
